claude_take: Today's set splits cleanly in two. On one side, Adobe, Anthropic and ElevenLabs are each racing to make AI more ambient, folded into your creative tools, your meetings, your audio, while Christopher Nolan is publicly asking studios to build the safeguards nobody has gotten around to yet. On the other, the institutions underneath all of that are visibly straining: Capri Holdings is replacing a 23-year CEO after back-to-back quarters of Michael Kors declines, Netflix's long-rumored studio-lot deal is heading to a foreclosure auction instead of a quiet handshake, and a new survey finds a clear majority of Americans now say the country itself is in decline. Nobody's panicking yet, but the pattern repeats across film, luxury and national mood alike: the old arrangements are being renegotiated faster than anyone is confidently replacing them.
claude_take_title: The Old Arrangements Are Being Renegotiated

items.headline: Adobe Turns Firefly Into an AI Creative Studio With Agents and Rival Models
items.summary: At Adobe MAX 2026, Adobe repositioned Firefly as a hub combining its own generative tools with a new Creative Agent and third-party models from Google, OpenAI, ByteDance and Kling, alongside an MCP connector so outside AI tools can plug directly into its apps. The move reshapes how creative professionals access competing AI providers, folding what used to require several separate subscriptions into one Adobe workflow.

items.headline: Anthropic Launches Claude Meetings, Putting an AI Participant Inside Google Meet Calls
items.summary: Anthropic introduced Claude Meetings in beta for Team and Enterprise plans, letting Claude join a Google Meet call as a visible participant that answers questions and builds plans and timelines live, alongside companion betas for Claude Whiteboards and Claude Sheets. Microsoft Teams and Zoom aren't supported yet, and early coverage flags open questions about what data Claude retains from a call and how reliable its drafts are in fast-moving discussions.

items.headline: ElevenLabs Ships Scribe v3 and Scribe v3 Live Transcription Models
items.summary: ElevenLabs released two new speech-to-text models, Scribe v3 for recorded audio and Scribe v3 Live for real-time audio, claiming 27% and 43% fewer word errors respectively than its previous v2 models across 102 languages. The update targets captioning and voice-agent pipelines, a less visible but increasingly load-bearing piece of production and creative-tooling infrastructure.

items.headline: Christopher Nolan Says Studios, Not the DGA, Must Lead on Blocking AI Training on Films
items.summary: As DGA president, Nolan said the guild cannot fully protect films from AI misuse because directors rarely hold the copyright themselves, so that responsibility falls to studios. He pointed to Universal's anti-AI-training language in 'The Odyssey' credits as a model other studios should copy, and criticized companies that lean on fair-use defenses to justify training on copyrighted film content.

items.headline: Netflix's Long-Rumored Radford Studio Deal Heads to a Foreclosure Auction Instead
items.summary: Goldman Sachs-led lenders have scheduled a November 24 foreclosure auction for Radford Studio Center, the Studio City lot Hackman Capital Partners bought for about $1.85 billion in 2021, seeking roughly $1.3 billion. The auction suggests Netflix's months-long negotiation to buy the lot directly has stalled, with the sale now set to run through a forced sale rather than the quiet deal long assumed to be close.

items.headline: Survey Finds Seven in Ten Americans Now Say the Country Is in Decline
items.summary: A Michigan State University American Communities Project survey of more than 2,100 adults, fielded in September and conducted by SSRS, found 70% of Americans now believe the country is in decline, sharply up from 55% a year earlier. Nearly half, 47%, said they are feeling real financial pain from rising prices, with concern about healthcare also climbing, a steep one-year shift in national mood that researchers plan to re-survey once the new Congress is seated.

items.headline: Capri Holdings Names Estée Lauder Veteran Justin Boxford CEO, Ending John Idol's 23-Year Run
items.summary: Capri Holdings, parent of Michael Kors and Jimmy Choo, named Justin Boxford, formerly Global President of Luxury Beauty Brands at Estée Lauder, as its next CEO effective January 4, 2027, succeeding John Idol after 23 years at the helm. Idol will stay on as a senior advisor through March 2027, and lead director Robin Freestone becomes independent chairman; the change lands as Capri's quarterly revenue fell 5.5% year over year, driven mainly by continued Michael Kors weakness even as Jimmy Choo grew.

items.headline: Mill's Harm Principle
items.headline_fr: Le principe de non-nuisance de Mill
items.summary: In 'On Liberty' (1859), John Stuart Mill argued that society may restrict a person's liberty only to prevent harm to others, never merely to protect that person from themselves or to enforce a majority's moral preferences. The principle underwrites much of modern liberal thought on free speech, drug policy and bodily autonomy, and remains the first move in almost every argument about where the law should and shouldn't reach into private life.
items.summary_fr: Dans De la liberté (1859), John Stuart Mill soutient que la société ne peut restreindre la liberté d'un individu que pour empêcher qu'il ne nuise à autrui, jamais simplement pour le protéger de lui-même ou imposer les préférences morales d'une majorité. Ce principe irrigue une grande partie de la pensée libérale moderne sur la liberté d'expression, les politiques en matière de drogues ou l'autonomie corporelle, et reste le premier argument invoqué dans presque tout débat sur les limites légitimes de la loi face à la vie privée.
